title: The icon preview timing test goes red again when the machine is busy
goal: One timing test reports a failure when the whole test suite runs on a machine that is also doing something else. It was fixed once for exactly this reason and has started doing it again. Every time it happens somebody has to work out for themselves whether the app got slower or the machine was busy, and a red run that means nothing is how a real slowdown gets ignored.
notes:
SEEN 2026-09-22, once, in a full run under deliberate load (12 spin processes plus a 24-thread on-device text recognition load, load average 16):

  Scripts/test.sh, 9112 tests, 728 suites, 215.0s, 2 issues
  X Test "A whole strip of moving previews fits inside one frame of the loop" recorded an issue at IconPreviewRenderTests.swift:249:38: Issue recorded

NOT reproduced on demand. The same test run on its own under the same load passes with room to spare:

  [perf] budget: moving icon previews, whole strip of 4 - 6.4ms on the calibration machine clock against a budget of 20ms (baseline 5.0ms x 2.5 tolerance). Read 8.2ms here beside a filter graph yardstick reading 10.1ms against its own 8.0ms, over 15 interleaved rounds

And the same full suite run idle, twice, reports only the separately filed export size flake. So it needs the whole suite AND a loaded machine together.

HISTORY: this exact test was fixed for this exact reason by the done task two-timing-tests-only-fail-when-the-whole-suite (shipped 8279e9b9, MachineSpeed.normalizedMS + checkInterleaved, Tests/PhotonzRenderTests/IconPreviewRenderTests.swift). Read that task log first: it records that a 5ms baseline plus the flat 8ms jitterSlackMS means this test only trips on a regression of about 4x, so whatever is moving here is moving a long way. That note is the obvious place to start.

RELATED, and a worked example of the shape of answer wanted: the-test-suite-stops-reporting-failures-that-are gave the text reading a way to say "this machine would not read" and made its suite skip with a reason instead of going red (Sources/PhotonzRender/TextReader.swift, recogniserHealth).
acceptance: The whole suite run on a deliberately loaded machine reports the same result for this test as the same suite run on an idle one, checked both ways at least twice
When the reading genuinely cannot be trusted the test says so rather than failing, the way the separated rows suite now does
The test still catches a real slowdown, proved by making the work slower on purpose and watching it go red

log.note: the export size flake your notes call separately filed had no task of its own: it is now an-animated-export-weighed-twice-comes-out-the-s, reproduced again 2026-09-23 in a full run (208988 vs 285616 bytes for the same short heic at High) and green in the same tree on a filter run and on a second full run
